utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Ekkehard Withopf, and the case manager, Kimberly Fleming.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel; Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and legal assistant. We would like to inform the Trial Chamber that in the Chamber -- in the courtroom we still have General Hadzihasanovic with us, and he asked me again to thank the Trial Chamber to be able to be present at his brother's funeral.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Defence of Mr. Kubura.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Mr. Rodney Dixon, Mr. Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We are going to go into private session, Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Withopf, you can continue with your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Withopf: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness XC. Witness --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XC, yesterday before the break you talked about your experiences in the Mehurici Elementary School. Can you please inform the Trial Chamber for how long you have been detained in the Mehurici Elementary School.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed, together with other civilians, up to 19th or 20th of June in the elementary school in Mehurici. That was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 19th or 20th of June, 1993, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Representatives of the International Red Cross came. They entered together with some soldiers and some civilian police. The soldiers and the civilian police read out a list with my name on it. They told us to step out of the building. The rest could stay in the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After this list had been read out and you were ordered to step out of the building, did you go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They took us to another building nearby. I found some detainees there. They were Croats. Among them there were some women and children. From there, they took some of the women and children into the sports hall, and we were accommodated in that building for a while. The Red Cross was there. They distributed ID cards amongst us in order to be able to identify us. They gave us pieces of paper in case we wanted to write to our family to let them know that we were alive and that we were there. After that, they took us to some sheds which had been used by the forestry office before the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XC, can you please inform the Trial Chamber how far these sheds have been away from the Mehurici Elementary School.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think some 200 or 300 metres, not more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness XC, can you please inform the Trial Chamber who took you to these sheds.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were taken there by the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go voluntarily to these sheds?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was already separated from my wife and children. They had stayed behind. They separated me and some others. I believe that there were some 25 of us. After a day or two, some were ordered to return; some new people were brought in. All in all, some 20 of us stayed on in those two sheds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform us about the ethnicity of the 20 or so people who stayed in these two sheds.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were all Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you been civilians or were these 20 individuals civilians or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always declared myself as a member of the HVO. That means I was a soldier. However, there were some elderly people amongst us. There were some handicapped people amongst us. There were even a miner person who was later on transferred to Kapelica to join with his father. In any case, some of us were soldiers, but some of us were also civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long have you been detained in the shed you were mentioning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 20th of June to the 4th or the 6th of July. I can't remember exactly. In any case, that's for how long we stayed in those sheds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the names of the other detainees who stayed with you in the shed? And for the time being, I wish you only to answer with yes or no, either yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I wish to like -- to go in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. We shall go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XC, can you please describe the living conditions in the shed you have been detained with the other people you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shed in which I was, there were 12 of us. It was a shed made of concrete, with a concrete floor. The size of the room was 3 by 3 metres. We had just one blanket. There were 12 of us. When we wanted to have a rest, we couldn't. We used a bucket as a toilet, and they would also let us use the nearby building as toilet. In the second shed where the others were, I was never there, but they told me that their conditions were even worse. They had to remain seated all the time. And if they wanted to stretch their legs, then they had to make room by one of them lying down and the other stretching their legs over that person. That's what they told me. I didn't see it myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XC, can you please inform the Trial Chamber for how long you and the other detainees had to live under such conditions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 20th of June to the 4th or 6th of July, 1993, I had to live like that. For some 15 days or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this also apply to the other detainees who were with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We all shared the same destiny. Sometimes during the day they would take us out of the shed to do some chores, but we were there all together all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this time period, Witness XC, have you or have the other detainees been taken out for questioning?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XC, you were mentioning that the persons which you detailed were taken to the school and beaten there. Just for clarification, which school are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The elementary school where we had been detained before and where the army members were on the upper-most floor, so the same school where the detainees were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to ask the Registrar to prepare the order to redact the name in line 25:1, as well as in line 12 and the following lines. These are the names which may reveal the identity of Witness XC. We are in open session, as we know. Mr. Withopf, can you please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XC, the individuals which were beaten in the Mehurici Elementary School, were they beaten in the building you yesterday made the marks on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm not sure what the witness said earlier; however, I've been following the transcript, and he was talking about the people being taken away. He didn't witness the situation. Later on he spoke about the fact that he must have learned subsequently, and that is that these people were beaten when the rifle and the money were not found. So I believe that the questions that the Prosecution is putting now is not based on what the witness knows personally or what he himself really saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, have you heard what the Defence has just said?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, it's certainly correct that the witness is making reference to facts he got to know from third persons; however, it is the position of the Prosecution that his evidence is admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. Would you please continue with your examination-in-chief. And I would also like to ask Mr. Registrar to make whatever is necessary to redact those lines which may identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please continue, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours. I'm actually very close to finishing the examination-in-chief of Witness XC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XC, you were informing the Trial Chamber that you have been detained until the 4th or 6th of June, I think -- unfortunately, I can't read it here any more. Can you please confirm for how long you have been detained.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on the 4th or 6th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer your question, I would like to say something else. On that date, when we were supposed to go, we didn't know where we were going. Some guys who were being taken out came back black and blue from beating. They probably knew that we were being transferred today and they made the most of that opportunity to beat us. On that day, they took us to a bus. We didn't know where we were being taken. Nobody wanted to tell us. They loaded us on the bus, and at one place we stopped, and that's where three other detained Croats joined us. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I think the witness named a number of individuals, and it needs to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Can we please redact lines in which names were mentioned, line 19, line 20, and Line 21, as well as the reference in line 22 which concerns the schoolmate of the witness. So, 20, 21, and 23. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XC, where have you finally been taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were taken to the prison in Zenica. We were registered there by the International Red Cross. And this prison was registered by the International Red Cross as a prison for prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does this prison in Zenica have a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Even before, it was called the Zenica KP Dom. I think that was still its name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness XC.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: This concludes the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Withopf. Before the Defence takes the floor for its cross-examination, there is a question I would like to put to you, Witness XC. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You told us that when you were detained in the school you were transferred to a shed, but that was after representatives of the Red Cross came to visit you in the school and the representatives of the Red Cross had a list of names. Can you confirm that the Red Cross representatives had a list of names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that the Red Cross had a list, but I said that the people, the civilian police, they read out that list before the Red Cross appeared. They appeared in front of the school. They read out the names of those people and took us to a different building. And the other detainees remained in that hall. The Red Cross visited us in that other building. When they took us there, that is where we were visited and were provided with these records, according to which we'd been registered with them, and they'd give us some sort of questionnaires to send to our parents, but they never came to pick them up. The Red Cross never came to pick these questionnaires up from us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for these details. You said that the civilian police had this list of names. The civilian police, as far as you're able to determine this, at the time who were they accountable to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know who they were accountable to, but there was cooperation between the civilian police, the army. Some of them had certain duties; others other duties. All I can say is there was cooperation between them, because the civilian police would take us to be questioned. For example, they escorted me to the village. So there was some kind of cooperation between them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How do you distinguish between the civilian and the military police? How can you differentiate them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the military police, on the whole they had white belts, whereas the civilian police had a different type of uniform. I can't remember what kind of uniform, what colour it was. But that's what helped us identify them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Having heard these additional details, the Defence may proceed with its cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness XC, good day. My name is Edina Residovic, and I'm representing General Hadzihasanovic. I would be grateful if you could answer some of my questions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go into private session? Because my -- the first couple of questions I have to ask might reveal the witness's identity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I was going to say. If the questions will be such that the witness will be providing names, yes, let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. XC, would it be correct to say that in April 1992 the Serbian army had already attacked and taken over the television transmitter which was on Mount Vlasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was a reason for the population to try to organise themselves in a military fashion in April 1992, in order to protect themselves and their area; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, that was a period during which the Croatian and Muslim population tried to organise themselves; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You in your village organised yourselves and you used the weapons that you yourselves had, and your Muslim neighbours in the village which was closest to you, Fazlici, did the same.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But Fazlici isn't the village closest to us. My first neighbours are Bosniaks who were about 200 metres from my house. So we organised ourselves and we tried to come to an agreement among ourselves and go on guard duty. So there were no problems of any kind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that in May or June 1992 Filip Balta, who was responsible for organising the people, established contact with the HVO Main Staff in Guca Gora, and then you became an HVO squad? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of 1993, structures were reorganised in various ways. So finally, in the spring of 1993, you became part of the newly founded Frankopan Brigade, whose headquarters were in Guca Gora. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From October 1992 --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we now go into private session. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll go back into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have several questions to ask you about a different matter now. In fact, in the course of the examination-in-chief, you said that in 1992 the presence of foreigners in the municipality of Travnik was noticed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The foreigners, whom you called the Mujahedin, in the autumn of 1992 were noticed in the area of Mehurici too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In July or August, that's when they were observed in the area of Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. I have to turn my microphone off when you are answering my questions, and that is what I was informed of. As you have already explained, these foreigners - that is to say, the Mujahedin - looked different, very different from the Croatian and Bosniak population. They were dark. They spoke a foreign language. They had beards, et cetera. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were aware of the fact that they had moved into an abandoned Serbian house in Poljanice, which is where they set up a camp, and they often went to Mehurici on market day. They left the house on such occasions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. But they weren't just in one house; there were several houses that they inhabited.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When passing through that area, you were able to see that those houses were guarded by the Mujahedin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I didn't pass through that part, but our detainees did and on that occasion, they saw that they were in those houses. But there was no need for me to pass through Poljanice. But people who had passed through Poljanice later saw them there, and it was common knowledge that that is where they had found accommodation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thanks. That explains it. Yesterday you said that part of the local Muslim population and refugees joined the Mujahedin and started emulating them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, you were able to observe that not only the Croats feared them, but many -- but many of the members of the army and the local population.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People were afraid of such men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the Mujahedin, in the autumn of 1992, for no apparent reason, as you said, passed rapidly through your village with a group of local young men, you went to the police station -- you went to the civilian police station in Mehurici and you drew the attention to this fact. You told the chief of the police of this fact. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, if my recollection is not completely wrong, the witness did not say that the Mujahedin passed rapidly through the village. The word "rapidly" is something which has been added by Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Antonetti, in response to your question, that's what the witness said. He said it seemed to be gymnastics of some kind. The witness can repeat what he said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they run through the village or did they linger in the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were doing gymnastics. They passed through the village. They stayed in the village for a short time. They returned again. You know, they were running slowly and crying out Arabic slogans, that sort of thing. That's the way they do gymnastics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think that this has clarified the matter, but that is the reason, in any event, for which you went to see the chief of the civilian place in Mehurici, and you drew his attention to this fact; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The chief of the civilian police at the time was Ferid Muhovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was Ferid and there was another person. I don't know if that was his name. But we turned to Ferid. I don't know whether he was the main or the deputy commander, but he was responsible there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He promised that he would do what he could; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd now like to discuss another subject. You said that up until spring 1993 you and members of your squad went to the front lines in Vlasic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Towards the end of 1992 and at the beginning of 1993, the joint task of the BH Army and the HVO was to protect the lines facing the Serbian forces and to fight the Serbian attackers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April 1993, you and members of your squad stopped going to the front lines in Vlasic and you started holding the lines, securing the lines around your village because of the conflicts that had broken out in the surroundings between the army and the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But that was a patrol in the village. It wasn't a line. These were village patrols that we were involved in. There weren't any lines in our village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, because of the large-scale conflicts in the Lasva Valley, the tension among the population in the village had increased, and that was the reason for which you organised yourselves differently; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You then received something against infantry mines from the command in Guca Gora; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only started laying the mines when we heard about the massacre in Miletici. Up until then, we only patrolled, went on patrol. But after we heard what had happened in Miletici, since there weren't many of us, we weren't able to provide security for the entire village, so we laid infantry mines on our ground and nowhere else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll now return to the events -- on the 7th of June, 1993, you received an order to return to Gornje Maljine, but you returned again because at the time the civilians had withdrawn from your village.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We returned that evening in order to patrol the village again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, on the 8th of June, in the morning, you received an order again according to which you should withdraw to Gornje Maljine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you reached the first houses in Maljine, you hid yourselves in a house, in one of the houses, in order to treat your father, who had been hit by the effect of a bullet ricochetting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. But it wasn't a house; it was a stable.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted). Most of all, he sat with us down there. Occasionally someone else would appear. But he was there. He remained there until they took us to Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He also requested that some young men, so to speak, some soldiers report to go to Gornje Maljine to protect the houses of Croat inhabitants from looters who had already started appearing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I remember his words very well, when he said, "Are there any honest men here? Twenty young men have looted our neighbour's houses, and where are our neighbours to return to?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I won't ask you in detail about what the Prosecution discussed with you, but I just want to check something. You said that while you were in the primary school -- in the primary school, they interrogated you on two occasions over a four-day period and you weren't mistreated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one beat me personally, because they knew me in that village. I was well known in Mehurici, both I and my wife, so no one really maltreated me much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were in the primary school, you got to know a member of

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I could add something: He was a member of the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And through him, you tried to find out what the fate of certain HVO soldiers was, HVO soldiers who had been captured and hadn't been brought to Mehurici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He told you that he too had escorted a group of detainees, that he'd been stopped in Poljanice by the Mujahedin, who put a knife to his throat and took some detainees from him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps for the sake of the previous witness, who had been granted protective measures, perhaps it might be a good idea to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask Madam Usher to accompany the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall continue this session until half past 10.00, when we are going to have our first break. Before we see the next witness, I would like to indicate that today the break has to last 30 minutes for technical reasons. We shall break at 10.30 and resume our session at 11.00. As for another point which has been raised, and that is that I've promised the Defence -- that I'm going to submit the statistical data on the protective measures for the witnesses. For the time being, out of the 19 witnesses, 5 have been granted protective measures, and that is 26.3 per cent. One-fourth of the witnesses so far have been granted protective measures. I would like to invite the Prosecution to tell us whether the witness is here and whether we can see the witness in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I would request to go into private session, since I will orally submit a motion for protective measures for the next witness. It's my understanding that the witness is available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In open session, the Chamber is retiring to deliberate on the issue that has been put forth. We are coming back in a minute or so. --- Break taken at 10.21 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session. I would kindly ask Mr. Registrar to move into public session -- into private session. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In open session, the Trial Chamber informs the interested parties that we shall now have our first break and that we shall resume at 11.00. We are inviting the Prosecution to tell us at 11.00 whether they want to tender the document that has just been mentioned. The Prosecution is going to tell us at 11.00, when we resume with our session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll resume now. And Mr. Registrar, could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Withopf:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness XD.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I please ask you to go back into private session, since my very first question may -- the answers to my very first questions may contain details that may identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, did there come a time in 1992 whilst you were working in Travnik when you saw foreigners arriving in this area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber at what point in time during the year 1992 it was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in March. It was at the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, Witness XD, what sort of foreigners you have seen arriving.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these people were different from the ones who lived down there. They were different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please explain to us what was the difference between the foreigners you have seen arriving and the people living in your area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were dark. They had beards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get to know from which countries these foreigners have been?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these foreigners speak the same language as the people in Travnik are speaking and spoke in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber, Witness XD, as to whether these foreigners wore uniforms.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these uniforms, have these uniforms been military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please, Witness XD, also inform the Trial Chamber as to whether these foreigners were armed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please tell us what sort of arms they had.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they had automatic rifles and knives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness XD, what sort of automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some kind of Kalashnikovs, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please inform us, Witness XD, what sort of knives they had.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends. Some of them were a little longer. They were sheathed, so I couldn't see them very well, but they were long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a certain word, Witness XD, you used whenever you talked about these foreigners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the word "Mujahedin"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I later found out that they were called the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For clarification, you later found out that these foreigners in military uniforms and having arms such as Kalashnikovs and long knives were referred to as Mujahedin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, the uniforms the Mujahedin wore in 1992, the Mujahedin you've seen in the area of Travnik in 1992, did these uniforms have any military insignia on them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please describe to the extent possible how these military insignia looked like.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were two sabres. There was something written in Arabic, and there was the sun and a book.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you, Witness XD, seen such Mujahedins also in the beginning of 1993 in the area of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's when I saw them the most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you recall, Witness XD, where in the beginning of 1993 you have seen the Mujahedin the most?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was near the mosque. I think it was in Osulje. There was a Medresa there, a school. And they were also seen in the cafe, where I worked. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The cafe in which you worked, was it located in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please inform the Trial Chamber where this location, Osulje, is situated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's right at the beginning of the entrance to Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, I'm now going to show you a board showing a number of military insignia. It's Prosecution Exhibit P4. And, Witness XD, it will appear on the screen in front of you. Do you see, Witness XD, the photo board with the military insignia in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, you have just a few minutes ago described the military insignia the Mujahedin were wearing in 1992 and 1993 in the area of Travnik as showing two sabres and something written in Arabic and there was the sun and a book.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to object because the witness did not state that the insignia were military insignia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness spoke about insignia on the uniform. Very well. Please rephrase your question more precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honour, the witness was making reference to the fact that the Mujahedin were wearing military uniforms, and I have asked him whether there were any insignia on such military uniforms. I think the only logical conclusion is these were military insignia. However, I'm going to ask the Witness XD the following:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The insignia you were describing a few minutes ago, do you see any of such one or even more of such insignia on the board in front of you that is similar or identical to the ones you have seen in 1992 and in the beginning of 1993 were worn by the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see a similar one. I'm not sure that it is an identical one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness XD, can you please identify the similar one you are referring to by telling the Trial Chamber the number which is shown on this photo board in front of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any other of the insignia you see in front of you which is similar or identical to the one -- to the ones you have seen the Mujahedin wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another similar one is number 22. The only difference is that this is an inscription in Arabic, instead of Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Very well. For the record, the Witness XD has identified on the Prosecution Exhibit P4 the military insignias number 1 and number 22 as being similar to the ones which have been worn by the Mujahedin in 1992 and in the beginning of 1993 in the area of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness XD. The Mujahedin, what was their relation with the local people in the area of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They moved around accompanied by local population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They moved around accompanied by local population. The local population you are referring to, Witness XD, were these civilians or were these soldiers or were these a mixture of both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Both means including local soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both civilians and soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the local soldiers, were these Muslims or Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness XD, to which army did the Muslim local soldiers belong to in the beginning of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Green Berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you inform the Trial Chamber, Witness XD, to which military formation the Green Berets you are referring to were later on transferred.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BiH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, how would you describe the situation in the area of Vitez and Travnik in the middle of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that it was tense.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please explain why you would say that the situation was tense.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the foreigners who caused that, and there had already been a conflict. A conflict had already broken out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For clarification, the foreigners who caused that, are these the foreigners you later on got to know that these were referred to as the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when fighting broke out between the ABiH and the HVO in your area, meaning in the area of Vitez and Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber when this actually happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was two months before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, "this was two months before." Before what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before a conflict broke out in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, for clarification purposes only, can you inform the Trial Chamber about the month when the conflict broke out in Vitez and in the area of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vitez and Travnik?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And if there is a distinction, could you please distinguish it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The time was not the same. It was in Novi Travnik that the conflict broke out first, and then Travnik followed after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, can you please tell us during which month in 1993 the conflict broke out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Vitez and in Travnik, I'm not sure. I believe that this was in March or in April.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter corrects herself: In the previous answer, the witness said that the conflict broke out in Novi Travnik first and then in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Witness XD, when you surrendered to the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you still have a recollection as to when this was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was on 18 or 19 September 1993 in Zabrdje, near Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please, Witness XD, provide us some more detail with respect to your surrender.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in trenches. An attack started around 2.00 in the afternoon. Two or three shells fell very close to my trench. An infantry attack followed after that. They came close to us and started throwing bombs into our trenches. The guy that was next to me in the trench, he got killed. I was wounded, and one guy came from one of the lower trenches to look for his co-fighters. He wanted to return, but as he was coming out of the trench they started shooting at him. They hit him in the legs. I pulled him back into the trench. A few more bombs were thrown into the trench. Some got activated; some didn't. And then they started shouting at us, asking us to surrender, which I did, eventually.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, you just informed us that on the 18th or the 19th of September, 1993 you surrendered to the ABiH. Do you still have a recollection as to which unit or members of which unit you surrendered?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were MOS members.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, "MOS," for what does it stand for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Muslim armed forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The members of the Muslim armed forces you surrendered to on the 18th or 19th of September, 1993, did they wear military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any military insignia on these uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the inscription "MOS" on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any further detail of the military insignia -- of the military insignia other with the -- other than the inscription "MOS"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two sabres and the inscription "MOS," and they were green.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall any further details of the military insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. After your surrender to MOS units of the ABiH, did there come a time when you have been brought to some barracks in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber as to how many days passed by between your capture on the 18th or 19th of September, 1993, and the day you have been brought to the barracks in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say with any certainty. I was in a very bad shape. I believe that it was five or six days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness XD, can you please briefly describe for the Trial Chamber what happened to you within these five or six days.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was captured and taken some 50 away from -- 50 metres away from the trench to an open field. All the fighters who had participated in the battle were gathered there. There were a number of them. The fighters bore the insignia of the BiH army. One of them that I knew from before ran up to me and kicked me; another one took a knife, ran up to me, but I pushed him away; then their commander intervened and told them to leave me alone. Then they took me to a little wood and ordered me to sit down. As I was sitting down, those who were passing by me kicked me. One of them allegedly recognised as a guard of a prison in Busovaca - although I had never been there - and he wanted to take his revenge on me. Then I was taken some 2 or 3 kilometres uphill to another open field. There I was administered first aid. They dressed the wounds on my face. My face was covered in blood. They gave me some water to drink. Then two guys came. I don't know who they were. They took me 50 metres away from that place and started interrogating me at gunpoint. They would put the barrel of their rifle into my mouth and against my forehead, threatening me and asking me to give them information that I couldn't give them, because I didn't know what to say. Then they took me back to the place where I had been administered first aid, and then I was put on a tractor and taken to the school in Tornica. While I was riding on the tractor, I was also beaten. And when I was in Tornica, they gathered around me. Some of them hit me and kicked me, and then I was taken for another interrogation. I wasn't beaten or ill-treated there, during that interrogation. And then I was taken to my cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, whilst you were riding on the tractor, you were beaten. The ones who beat you, were they soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were they soldiers of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were informing us, Witness XD, that five to six days after your surrender to MOS units of the ABiH on 18th or 19th of September, 1993, you were finally brought to some barracks in Travnik. Witness XD, I'm now showing you a photograph. And this photograph will appear on the screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And the Prosecution, for the information of Your Honours and Defence counsel, will provide hard copies of this photograph at a later point during today's proceedings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, can you please tell us what you can see on the photograph in front of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a building within the barracks compound where I was detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, Witness XD, as to whether this is a military barracks which has been used prior to the war by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that. It was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please clarify for the Trial Chamber as to whether this is the military barracks you have been brought to five or six days after your surrender on the 18th or 19th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, once the hard copies of this photograph is available, we intend to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, were these soldiers of the ABiH who brought you to the former JNA barracks in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you arrived in the former JNA barracks in Travnik, where have you been taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They brought me to the entrance. Then I descended down a flight of stairs. There were two guards there. They took my first and my last names there and made a note of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The two guards who were there and took your first and your last name, were these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They wore uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the uniforms they wore, were they ABiH uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, after you have been registered, meaning that your first and your last name was taken and the note of that has been made, where have you been brought to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took me to a cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This cell, where in the building of the former JNA barracks, where was this cell situated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have a recollection, Witness XD, whether there have been other cells in the basement different from the one you have been taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were four cells all together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please describe for the Trial Chamber how these cells were situated in relation to each other.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were next to each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform us about the size of the cells.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 6 by 4 metres or 4 by 5 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, I will now show you - and again on the screen in front of you - a further photograph, and copies of this photograph will be made available to both the Chamber and Defence counsel in due course. Witness XD, what do you see on the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the corridor and the cells where I was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were brought to one of these cells, Witness XD. Were there already any further detainees in the cell you were brought to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were some detained Muslims there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get to know, Witness XD, that the other individuals detained in the prison cell you have been brought to were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I introduced myself to them and vice versa. And some of them I knew from before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these Muslim detainees or some of them wear any military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some did; some didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the ones who actually wore military uniforms, were these military uniforms of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you were put in the prison cell together with the ABiH soldiers which were detained there, what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't maltreated there at all, and then they transferred me to another cell. I was right next to this cell, and there were Muslims there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber how many Muslims were in the first cell you were detained.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it varied. Between seven and ten. One day two would appear, and two or three would leave. So there were people coming and going.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please inform the Trial Chamber as to how many Muslims were detained in the second cell you were imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About ten people in the second cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Muslims in the second cell, were they soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the soldiers in the second cell, members of which army were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BH Army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you get to know this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, by talking to them. And on the basis of the uniforms that they were wearing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For verification, the uniforms they were wearing, were these ABiH uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Witness XD, when you have been transferred to another cell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the cell in which the Croatian people had been detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Croatian people which were detained in the third cell, were these soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were soldiers, but one of them was a civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For clarification, were they HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many detainees were in the third cell you have been transferred to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that cell, there were nine of us. First of all, there were nine of us, and then others arrived later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The others who arrived later, were they also Croat soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were. But I wasn't with them. I was transferred to another prison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The size of the third cell you were imprisoned, was it identical or similar to the size of the first cell you have been imprisoned with the Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Similar. It was similar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber for how long you have been detained in the first cell with the ABiH soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, a few days in the first cell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please inform the Trial Chamber for how long you have been detained in the second cell, again with the ABiH soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent a day in the second cell. I spent the night there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please inform the Trial Chamber for how long you have been detained in the cell with the HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about six months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, I'm now going to ask you whether you still recall the names of the other Croat detainees. And for the time being, I ask you to only respond by either yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will now go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, you were mentioning a few minutes ago that you haven't been beaten in the first cell. Did there come a time during your detention in the former JNA barracks in Travnik when you have been beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please go into some detail in that respect.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was in the morning, when we were supposed to go and wash. In fact, we had to go to the toilets. We had to go up a flight of stairs. And usually BH Army troops would wait for us there, the troops who slept over at the barracks. They'd wait for us in order to give us a bit of a beating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any beatings in respect to the other Croat detainees?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The others fared worse than I did. I can say that I fared quite well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other Croat detainees fared worse than you did. Can you please provide us with some more detail in respect to the fact that they fared worse than you did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, individuals were able to get out of it. Guards would prevent beatings. So we would rush into the cells while others were on the floor because they didn't manage to get out in time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Witness XD, do you still recall whether the ones who beat you and the other detainees were members of a particular ABiH unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were these members of the Coyotes, the Black Coyotes, as they were called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you have a recollection of another particular unit which has been involved in the beatings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever hear, Witness XD, of a military unit called Krajisnici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, they were all members of the Krajisnici. They were all Krajisnici people on the grounds of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know, Witness XD, who has been the commander of the Krajisnici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Alagic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know, Witness XD, where this commander named Alagic had his headquarters at the time you have been detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, across the road from our prison, 50 to 60 metres away there was a building there, and rumour had it that he was billeted in that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the time of your detention, of your six-month detention in the former JNA barracks in Travnik, did there come a time when you have been taken out for whatever reason?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please explain us for what reasons you have been taken out.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was taken out for a trial. And we also went to do work; for example, if a central heating pipe broke, we had to repair it. So there was work we had to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Coming back to the ABiH soldiers which were detained together with you in the first cell and in the second cell, do you know, Witness XD, why these ABiH soldiers have been detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because of theft, murder, desertion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get to know that these ABiH soldiers were detained in the former JNA barracks in Travnik because of theft, murder, and desertion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because people speak about everything in the cells. Everything was known.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that the ABiH soldiers detained together with you told you about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If my recollection isn't wrong, you said there were some ten ABiH soldiers in the first cell and some ten ABiH soldiers in the second cell. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these 20 ABiH soldiers -- about 20 ABiH soldiers all detained for the reasons you just mentioned, namely, theft, murder, and desertion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you get to know about this fact because they told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by listening to them speaking to each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Witness XD, when you got to know a bit more about the crimes for which they were detained in the JNA barracks in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for some individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please share with us the knowledge you have about these individuals.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those who were there for murder, yes, they were there for murder and then for black marketeering, for theft, stealing flour, for fleeing from the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there anything else you got to know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The ones who have been detained in the JNA barracks in Travnik, the former JNA barracks in Travnik, for murder, did you get to know about any details in respect to the murders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you, Witness XD, ever been informed why you have been detained in the former JNA barracks in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for extremist action within the HVO, allegedly; simply on the basis of the fact that I was an HVO member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you get to know, Witness XD, that there was an allegation against you for extremist action within the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because I went to court to be tried.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us to which court you went to be tried.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a military court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please tell us where this military court has been situated.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you go to the military court in Travnik during the time you have been detained in the former JNA barracks in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the barracks, and afterwards, when I was transferred to this other place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the month when you have been or when you went to the Travnik military court?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time was in December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For clarification --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- was it December 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are saying it was the first time in December 1993. Did there come a second time when you went to the Travnik military court in the course of your detention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then I received a decision on the extension of my time in detention.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The witness didn't say that he went there the first time in December. He said he went to trial in December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber has taken note of this comment. The Prosecution should rephrase the question to ask him whether he went to the military court before the month of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I refer to the transcript. The question has been: "Do you recall the month when you have been or when you went to the Travnik military court." And the answer has been: "The first time --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, the transcript is in English. It seems that the Defence heard the witness's answer in the B/C/S language, and according to his answer in the B/C/S language it doesn't tally with the English version. Witness XD, when you went to the military court, you were -- you went there in December. But did you go before the month December.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first time you went to the military court was in the month of December, then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was in the month of December. That's when I received -- I've received a decision, and I think it is noted in the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you only went there once? Or did you go there several times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Later I went again. I was first given decisions about the extension of my period of detention, for 30 or 40 days, and then I went to trial, where they appointed Defence counsel for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It seems that he went there in December and later on several other times, but perhaps he doesn't remember things very clearly. We have another five minutes before the break, Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The decisions, Witness XD, you received, did you receive them in written?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you receive them in the course of your detention in the former JNA barracks in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not the last one. Since there was an exchange, they released me then, and I don't know what the outcome of everything was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you still recall the decisions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the decisions about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, about extremist action, since I was an HVO member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And has there ever been a judgement following the trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had to appoint a lawyer to go to Travnik to see what had happened and what the outcome was. The lawyer brought me the judgement, according to which I'd been granted amnesty. That's how this matter ended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, you were talking about Muslim ABiH soldiers detained in the former JNA barracks for a number of reasons you detailed a few minutes ago. Do you recall as to whether these detainees - the ABiH soldier detainees - had to go to trial as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, some of them did have to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, it's now almost 12.30. I would suggest to take the break now. I anticipate finishing the examination-in-chief within 20 or so minutes after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's half past 12.00. We'll have a break until five to 1.00. We will then resume at five to 1.00, and we will continue until 1.45. I hope that the Defence will have the time to proceed with its cross-examination. Witness, we're going to have a 25-minute break now. You can have a rest. And we will resume in 25 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have three-quarters of an hour to finish the examination-in-chief and to start the cross-examination. We shall start with the examination-in-chief by the Prosecution. Are we in open session, Mr. Registrar? Mr. Withopf, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, just before the break, you were informing the Trial Chamber that some of the ABiH soldiers who were detained together with you in the JNA barracks in Travnik had also to go to trial. What happened to the ones who had not to go to trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some volunteered to go into combat. Two went to Bucici. One of them was killed there and the other one was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, do you have any knowledge about other Croats detained together with you during this time period who were facing the same or similar allegations as you were facing at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not all of them did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not all of them did. But were there some who actually did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness XD, I'm now going to ask you a question. Will you please for the time being only say yes or no. Do you know the names of the other Croat detainees who faced the same allegations as you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS XC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President. Cross-examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, you now have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could use this opportunity -- we now got the copies of the photographs -- to actually tender these photographs in order to formally conclude the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is going to take a few minutes, because the photographs had -- have to be marked, the witness has to put his name on the photos. It will take some time. Madam Usher, can you please give the two photos to the witness. Witness, you're going to put your name and the date of birth on these photos. We are going to do it in private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to complete my cross-examination in the time that you have given me. But just for the record, I would like to state that the Prosecution had an hour for this witness. Cross-examined by Ms. Residovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. XD. My name is Edina Residovic. I am Defence counsel for General Hadzihasanovic. I'm going to ask you to answer a few questions. I --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to go back into private session, please, in order to protect the identity of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will turn to the Prosecution. Could you confirm that we will have one or several witnesses tomorrow, and can you tell us whether there are any difficulties or not and whether or not this witness has arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have one -- we will have one witness tomorrow and we will have two witnesses on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So we will have one witness tomorrow, and on Friday we will have two witnesses. Are there any comments that the Defence would like to make before we adjourn? No comments? No comments from the Prosecution either? So as we have covered everything today, we will adjourn, and I will see you all tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of January, 2004, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.43 p.m.,
